# ghx command reference

Every command prints one JSON document (or a spill result). Errors are `{"error":{"code","message","hint","details"}}` with a non-zero exit. `ghx <cmd> --help` and `ghx <cmd> --schema` print the same information as JSON.

- [`ghx ci rerun`](#ghx-ci-rerun) (write): Rerun failed jobs of completed runs on the PR head, or of one run (--flaky: only likely-flaky jobs)
- [`ghx ci retrigger`](#ghx-ci-retrigger) (write): Fire fresh pull_request workflows by closing and reopening the PR (never left closed)
- [`ghx ci wait`](#ghx-ci-wait) (read): Wait for CI on a PR, branch or run; one JSON summary, exit code = outcome (run in background)
- [`ghx ci why`](#ghx-ci-why) (read): Why CI is red: failing jobs, step, tests, errors, log path, shared-with-main and flake
- [`ghx doctor`](#ghx-doctor) (read): Check the setup: gh version and features, auth, git, the target repo and its config.
- [`ghx hook claude-pretooluse`](#ghx-hook-claude-pretooluse) (read): Claude Code PreToolUse hook: background ghx ci wait, steer raw gh to ghx (stdin protocol)
- [`ghx init`](#ghx-init) (write): Write a starter .github/ghx.json (components inferred from the workspace).
- [`ghx install`](#ghx-install) (write): Install the Claude Code hook and CLAUDE.md block, plus deny rules at project scope (try --dry-run).
- [`ghx pr comment`](#ghx-pr-comment) (write): Post a typed coordination comment: note, merge precondition, status or supersede
- [`ghx pr create`](#ghx-pr-create) (write): Open a PR from validated JSON: compact body, hidden ghx block, exact read-back
- [`ghx pr edit`](#ghx-pr-edit) (write): Patch a ghx PR: re-validated, block rev+1, retarget or draft toggle, exact read-back
- [`ghx pr feedback`](#ghx-pr-feedback) (read): All PR feedback (reviews, findings, comments, bots), filterable; full bodies in a file
- [`ghx pr land`](#ghx-pr-land) (write): Wait until mergeable, then merge pinned to that head (run like ci wait)
- [`ghx pr merge`](#ghx-pr-merge) (write): Merge when policy allows, pinned to the evaluated head; every blocker reported together
- [`ghx pr ready`](#ghx-pr-ready) (write): Mark a PR ready for review, or back to draft with --undo; any PR, no ghx block needed
- [`ghx pr resolve`](#ghx-pr-resolve) (write): Set the status of findings or preconditions (append-only event; resolves the review thread)
- [`ghx pr review`](#ghx-pr-review) (write): Post a review: verdict, inline findings in the diff, hidden blocks, pinned to the head
- [`ghx pr status`](#ghx-pr-status) (read): One object: description, block, merge readiness, CI for the head, feedback, preconditions, stack
- [`ghx uninstall`](#ghx-uninstall) (write): Remove what ghx install added to Claude Code settings and CLAUDE.md (try --dry-run).
- [`ghx version`](#ghx-version) (read): Print the ghx version, Node version and platform (no gh calls).

## Passthrough reads

These gh reads run through ghx in a bounded JSON envelope (`{passthrough:{argv, exitCode, json|text|stdoutPath, stdoutBytes, stderr}}`): `ghx pr diff`, `ghx pr list`, `ghx issue view`, `ghx issue list`, `ghx search issues`, `ghx search prs`, `ghx search code`, `ghx search repos`, `ghx search commits`, `ghx release list`, `ghx release view`, `ghx repo view`, `ghx workflow list`, `ghx workflow view`, `ghx run list`, `ghx run view`, `ghx run download`, `ghx label list`, `ghx api`. `api` is GET only; `run view` without `--log`; `run download` needs `-D <dir>`. Commands ghx wraps (`gh pr view`, `gh pr checks`, `gh run view --log`, `gh pr merge`, …) are refused with the exact replacement; other writes are refused.

## ghx ci rerun

Rerun failed jobs of completed runs on the PR head, or of one run (--flaky: only likely-flaky jobs)

`ghx ci rerun <target> [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 2m (max 5m).

Reruns the failed jobs of completed Actions runs for the current PR head, or of one run (run:<id>, for CI without a PR, such as main). The run id pins a run target to its commit; --expect-head checks it. Runs still in progress are skipped (RUN_IN_PROGRESS) and runs at ci.maxRerunAttempts (RERUN_LIMIT, default 3). --job reruns matching jobs; --flaky only jobs with flake evidence (NO_FLAKY_CANDIDATES if none), never widening to a real failure: one job per run at a time, the rest DEFERRED until that run completes. A run GitHub rejected before any job ran is never rerun (WORKFLOW_INVALID): fix the file and push. A rerun reuses the original merge ref: after a base change, use ghx ci retrigger.

Flags:

- `--job <string>` (repeatable): Only failed jobs whose name matches (repeatable; * and ?)
- `--flaky` (default `false`): Only jobs whose flake score is medium or higher
- `--expect-head <string>`: Refuse with HEAD_MOVED unless the head (for run:<id>, the run's commit) is this SHA
- `--override <string>` (repeatable): RERUN_LIMIT: rerun past ci.maxRerunAttempts
- `--reason <string>`: Why the override is allowed (who asked); required with --override

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Replaces: `gh run rerun <run-id>`, `gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`, `gh run rerun <run-id> --job`.

Examples:

- `ghx ci rerun powerhouse-inc/powerhouse#3301 --flaky`: Rerun only the jobs that look flaky
- `ghx ci rerun 3301`: Rerun every failed job of the completed runs on the head
- `ghx ci rerun 3301 --job 'Test Reactor*'`: Rerun matching failed jobs
- `ghx ci rerun run:40345582950 -R owner/repo`: Rerun the failed jobs of one run (main, no PR)
- `ghx ci rerun 3301 --override RERUN_LIMIT --reason "user asked in chat"`: Past ci.maxRerunAttempts

Schema: `ghx ci rerun --schema`.

## ghx ci retrigger

Fire fresh pull_request workflows by closing and reopening the PR (never left closed)

`ghx ci retrigger <pr> [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 3m (max 10m).

Closes and reopens the PR so GitHub runs its pull_request workflows on the current merge ref (a rerun reuses the old one). Refuses unless the PR is open, its head and base branches exist and you authored it (AUTHOR_NOT_VIEWER, overridable). A failed reopen is retried, then REOPEN_FAILED. Afterwards it looks for new check suites on the head for --wait-for-runs (default 60s) and warns NO_NEW_RUNS if none appear.

Flags:

- `--expect-head <string>`: Refuse with HEAD_MOVED unless the head is this SHA
- `--wait-for-runs <string>` (default `"60s"`): How long to look for new check suites after the reopen (e.g. 60s, 2m; max 5m)
- `--override <string>` (repeatable): AUTHOR_NOT_VIEWER: retrigger someone else's PR
- `--reason <string>`: Why the override is allowed (who asked); required with --override

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Replaces: `gh pr close <n> && gh pr reopen <n>`.

Examples:

- `ghx ci retrigger powerhouse-inc/powerhouse#3301`: Close and reopen to fire pull_request CI
- `ghx ci retrigger 3301 --expect-head 9f2c4e1`: Refuse if the head moved
- `ghx ci retrigger 3169 --override AUTHOR_NOT_VIEWER --reason "user asked in chat"`: Someone else's PR, when the user asked

Schema: `ghx ci retrigger --schema`.

## ghx ci wait

Wait for CI on a PR, branch or run; one JSON summary, exit code = outcome (run in background)

`ghx ci wait <targets…> [flags]`

read, stream, no deadline.

Run `ghx ci wait <pr>` with the Bash tool and `run_in_background: true`. Then continue other work or end your turn. Do not poll, sleep, or use Monitor for CI. You will be re-invoked when it exits. Its stdout is the full answer and its exit code is the outcome. In a subagent, which cannot end its turn and be woken, run it in the foreground with --foreground (the ghx hook adds it, with the 10-minute Bash timeout): it returns within 9 minutes, and on exit 15 you re-run the identical command, which resumes from the saved state. The summary is never spilled: it is compacted to 16 KB, and --max-bytes and GHX_MAX_BYTES are ignored.

Flags:

- `--until <first-failure|settled|mergeable>` (default `"first-failure"`): first-failure: return at the first new failure or settled green; settled: wait for everything; mergeable: settled, then the merge CI gate (PR targets only; a branch or run is a usage error)
- `--any` (default `false`): Return when the first target reaches a terminal state
- `--on-head-change <restart|stop|stay>`: On a head change: restart (PR default), stop (exit 12) or stay (branch default)
- `--check <string>` (repeatable): Only checks whose name matches (repeatable; globs); under --until mergeable, required checks always count
- `--diagnose` (default `true`): Diagnose each failure as it lands; --no-diagnose skips it
- `--compare-main` (default `true`): Compare failures with the default branch; --no-compare-main skips it
- `--stream` (default `false`): Print every event as NDJSON (for humans; agents use the default)
- `--expect-head <string>`: One PR: judge CI only once its head is this SHA or has moved past it (default: the local HEAD when the cwd is on the PR branch and pushed)
- `--foreground` (default `false`): Return pending (exit 15) after 9 min, under the Bash tool cap: for a foreground call in a subagent; re-run the identical command

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Replaces: `gh pr checks --watch`, `gh run watch <run-id>`, `gh pr checks`, `gh run list`.

Examples:

- `ghx ci wait 3301 -R powerhouse-inc/powerhouse`: Run with run_in_background: true
- `ghx ci wait owner/repo#12 --until settled`: Wait for every check, not the first failure
- `ghx ci wait owner/repo#12 --expect-head 9f2c4e1`: After a push: judge CI on 9f2c4e1, not the old head
- `ghx ci wait owner/repo#12 --until mergeable`: Settled CI, then the merge CI gate
- `ghx ci wait branch:main@9f2c4e1 -R owner/repo`: CI for one commit on a branch
- `ghx ci wait run:40345582950 --until settled -R owner/repo`: One workflow run until it completes (e.g. after ghx ci rerun run:<id>)
- `ghx ci wait owner/repo#12 owner/repo#13 --any`: Return at the first target that finishes
- `ghx ci wait --foreground owner/repo#12 --until mergeable`: In a subagent: foreground, returns within 9 min; re-run on exit 15

Schema: `ghx ci wait --schema`.

## ghx ci why

Why CI is red: failing jobs, step, tests, errors, log path, shared-with-main and flake

`ghx ci why [<target>] [flags]`

read, single document, timeout 2m (max 5m).

Diagnoses the failing checks on a PR head, one workflow run (run:<id>; --run is the same), one job (job:<id>), or a branch head (branch:<name>: every workflow's newest run on the branch's head commit) in one call. Logs come from the jobs API, so a finished job is diagnosed while the rest of its run is still going. Full logs are written to files (logPath). Green jobs whose ci.keySteps step was skipped are listed in suspicious.

Flags:

- `--run <string>`: A workflow run id or URL (the same as run:<id>)
- `--job <string>` (repeatable): Only failing jobs whose name matches (repeatable; * and ?)
- `--compare-main` (default `true`): Compare failures with the default branch; --no-compare-main skips it
- `--max-jobs <integer>` (default `5`): Failing jobs to diagnose
- `--excerpt-lines <integer>` (default `20`): Log excerpt lines per job

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Replaces: `gh run view <run-id> --log`, `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`, `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/actions/jobs/{id}/logs`.

Examples:

- `ghx ci why 3301 -R powerhouse-inc/powerhouse`: Diagnose the failing checks on PR #3301
- `ghx ci why owner/repo#12 --job 'Test*'`: Only jobs whose name starts with Test
- `ghx ci why run:37948190914 -R owner/repo`: One workflow run, without a PR
- `ghx ci why job:51234567890 -R owner/repo`: One job (gh run view --job <id> --log-failed)
- `ghx ci why branch:main -R owner/repo`: Is main red, and why: every workflow on its head
- `ghx ci why 12 --no-compare-main`: Skip the comparison with the default branch

Schema: `ghx ci why --schema`.

## ghx hook claude-pretooluse

Claude Code PreToolUse hook: background ghx ci wait, steer raw gh to ghx (stdin protocol)

`ghx hook claude-pretooluse`

read, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

Reads the PreToolUse event JSON on stdin (the one command that does; Claude Code delivers it there) and prints a hook reply or nothing. A Bash `ghx ci wait` without run_in_background gets updatedInput with run_in_background: true and no permission decision, in any repo. The rest applies only when the event's cwd is in a checkout with .github/ghx.json (found by walking up to .git; no gh or git spawn): a raw gh write ghx wraps (gh pr merge, gh -R o/r pr create, …) gets permissionDecision deny in every mode, and a gh CI polling loop (Bash or Monitor) or a gh read ghx wraps gets permissionDecision deny (GHX_HOOK_MODE=deny|ask|off; default deny), each naming the ghx replacement. Elsewhere gh calls get no output. Fails open: any error, unparseable stdin or a missing cwd exits 0 with no output. No gh calls. Register it with matcher Bash|Monitor (docs/agents/hooks.md).

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Examples:

- `ghx hook claude-pretooluse`: Run by Claude Code with the event on stdin; settings: matcher "Bash|Monitor"

Schema: `ghx hook claude-pretooluse --schema`.

## ghx init

Write a starter .github/ghx.json (components inferred from the workspace).

`ghx init [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

Components come from --component (repeatable), else package.json workspaces / pnpm-workspace.yaml, else top-level directories. They take the names the git log uses as commit scopes (type(scope): …) where a directory or package name matches, with the other names as aliases; a nested package stays part of its parent unless the log scopes it. Refuses to overwrite without --force; --dry-run returns the config without writing.

Flags:

- `--component <string>` (repeatable): Component name (repeatable); skips inference
- `--force` (default `false`): Overwrite an existing config

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Examples:

- `ghx init --dry-run`
- `ghx init --component reactor --component codegen`

Schema: `ghx init --schema`.

## ghx install

Install the Claude Code hook and CLAUDE.md block, plus deny rules at project scope (try --dry-run).

`ghx install [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

User scope edits $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (else ~/.claude)/settings.json and CLAUDE.md, adding the hook and the block but no deny rules: deny rules cannot be conditional, and the hook enforces only in repos with .github/ghx.json. A user-scope re-install removes deny rules an earlier ghx install added (warning INSTALL_DENY_REMOVED) and never the ones you added. Project scope edits .claude/settings.local.json (per machine, uncommitted) and CLAUDE.md at the git toplevel, and also merges the gh write deny rules (--no-deny skips them). Warns SETTINGS_LOCAL_NOT_IGNORED when git would not ignore that file. Keeps every other setting, backs up each changed file to <config dir>/ghx-install/<scope>-<hash>/backups/<name>.bak-ghx-<time> (never into the repo; files[].backup gives each path) beside the record of what it added, and writes atomically. The hook runs this ghx by absolute path. Run from npx, it first runs npm i -g @thegoldenmule/ghx@<this version> and hands the install to that global copy (handoff); --no-global refuses instead. Re-running updates in place; --dry-run returns unified diffs and writes nothing. Undo: ghx uninstall.

Flags:

- `--scope <user|project>` (default `"user"`): user (~/.claude) or project (repo .claude/settings.local.json)
- `--deny`: Project scope: merge the gh write deny rules (default); --no-deny skips them. User scope never adds them
- `--hook` (default `true`): Register the PreToolUse hook; --no-hook skips it
- `--snippet` (default `true`): Add the CLAUDE.md block; --no-snippet skips it
- `--bin-dir <string>`: Also symlink <dir>/ghx to bin/ghx.js (recorded, so uninstall removes it without the flag)
- `--hook-mode <ask|deny>`: ask sets env.GHX_HOOK_MODE=ask; deny removes it (the default mode)
- `--global` (default `true`): From npx: install ghx globally first (default); --no-global refuses instead

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Examples:

- `ghx install --dry-run`: Show the diffs first
- `ghx install --bin-dir ~/.local/bin`
- `ghx install --scope project --no-snippet`

Schema: `ghx install --schema`.

## ghx pr comment

Post a typed coordination comment: note, merge precondition, status or supersede

`ghx pr comment <pr> [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

Write {kind, …} with your file tool and pass --input c.json. Kinds: note {body}; precondition {condition: {type: pr-merged|release-includes, ref} | {type: manual, text}}; status {state, body, refs?}; supersede {by}. Refs must exist and not be this PR. --close closes the PR (not with a precondition); on someone else's PR it is AUTHOR_NOT_VIEWER unless --override AUTHOR_NOT_VIEWER --reason.

Flags:

- `--close` (default `false`): Close the PR after commenting (not with a precondition)
- `--override <string>` (repeatable): AUTHOR_NOT_VIEWER: --close someone else's PR
- `--reason <string>`: Why the override is allowed (who asked); required with --override

JSON-only fields: `kind`, `body`, `condition`, `state`, `refs`, `by`.

Input: JSON input is required: write it to a file, then ghx pr comment --input file.json (or --input -).

Replaces: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr close --comment`.

Examples:

- `ghx pr comment octo/demo#7 --input -`: or --input c.json
- `ghx pr comment 7 --input note.json`: {"kind":"note","body":"…"}
- `ghx pr comment 7 --input s.json --close`: {"kind":"supersede","by":"#9"}, then close

Schema: `ghx pr comment --schema`.

## ghx pr create

Open a PR from validated JSON: compact body, hidden ghx block, exact read-back

`ghx pr create [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 2m (max 10m).

ghx pr create --example prints a valid input for this repo; write it to pr.json, edit it, and pass --input pr.json. Required: title, description, testing, risk, revertPolicy. base and head default to the default and current branch; components the diff touches are added (past 5, ghx records the rest as alsoTouched); draft and stackedOn follow the base. Validation runs before any write and reports every issue at once (VALIDATION); DUPLICATE_PR when the head already has an open PR.

Flags:

- `--example`: Print a valid input for this repo (its component names) and the rules
- `--batch`: Create several PRs from {defaults, items}

JSON-only fields: `title`, `description`, `testing`, `risk`, `riskNote`, `components`, `revertPolicy`, `revertNote`, `revertWith`, `base`, `head`, `draft`, `refs`, `defaults`, `items`.

Input: JSON-only fields go in --input file.json (or --input -); flags and positionals cover the rest.

Replaces: `gh pr create`.

Examples:

- `ghx pr create -R octo/demo --input -`: or --input pr.json
- `ghx pr create --example`: a valid input for this repo, with its component names and the rules
- `ghx pr create --input pr.json --dry-run`: preview the rendered body without creating
- `ghx pr create --batch --input prs.json`: several PRs: {defaults, items}; stacked items in order

Schema: `ghx pr create --schema`.

## ghx pr edit

Patch a ghx PR: re-validated, block rev+1, retarget or draft toggle, exact read-back

`ghx pr edit [<pr>] [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 2m (max 10m).

Write the patch with your file tool and pass --input patch.json; only the fields to change (ghx pr edit --example shows one). Every issue comes back at once (VALIDATION), before any write. DESCRIPTION_DRIFT when the visible text was edited in the UI (include it, or --discard-ui-edits); {"draft": …} or {"base": …} alone works on any PR; other fields on a PR without a ghx block are NO_BLOCK unless "adopt": true with the full object. components follows pr create: past 5 touched, the 5 primary ones (ghx records the rest). GH_FORBIDDEN unless you have write access or opened the PR yourself (GitHub lets authors edit their own PRs). CONCURRENT_EDIT when the title or body changed since the read; GitHub has no If-Match, so an edit made in the moment between the final re-read and the PATCH is still overwritten.

Flags:

- `--discard-ui-edits`: Proceed when the visible description or title was edited outside ghx; the block wins
- `--example`: Print an example patch and the rules for this repo

JSON-only fields: `title`, `description`, `testing`, `risk`, `riskNote`, `components`, `revertPolicy`, `revertNote`, `revertWith`, `base`, `draft`, `refs`, `adopt`.

Input: JSON-only fields go in --input file.json (or --input -); flags and positionals cover the rest.

Replaces: `gh pr edit`.

Examples:

- `ghx pr edit octo/demo#12 --input -`: or --input patch.json
- `ghx pr edit --example`: an example patch and the rules for this repo
- `ghx pr edit 12 --input patch.json --dry-run`: preview the rendered body without editing
- `ghx pr ready 12`: mark it ready for review (any PR; --undo converts back to draft)

Schema: `ghx pr edit --schema`.

## ghx pr feedback

All PR feedback (reviews, findings, comments, bots), filterable; full bodies in a file

`ghx pr feedback <pr> [flags]`

read, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

Folds issue comments, reviews and inline threads into reviews, findings, comments and bots; unstructured items are kept with structured:false. --open keeps what still needs action. Bodies are capped at 2,000 chars inline; artifactPath holds the same document with every body in full.

Flags:

- `--open` (default `false`): Only what is still open: open findings, unresolved human threads, unmet preconditions, change requests
- `--source <ghx|human|bot>`: Only ghx (structured), human or bot items
- `--since <string>`: Only items newer than an ISO time or a commit SHA's date
- `--include-outdated` (default `false`): With --open, keep findings on outdated lines too (one that blocks merge is always kept)

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Replaces: `gh pr view --comments`, `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/comments`, `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/comments`.

Examples:

- `ghx pr feedback 3301 -R powerhouse-inc/powerhouse --open`: What is still open on #3301
- `ghx pr feedback owner/repo#12 --source human`: Only human, unstructured feedback
- `ghx pr feedback 12 --since 9f2c4e1`: Only feedback newer than that commit

Schema: `ghx pr feedback --schema`.

## ghx pr land

Wait until mergeable, then merge pinned to that head (run like ci wait)

`ghx pr land <pr> [flags]`

write, stream, no deadline.

ci wait --until mergeable, then pr merge, in one call. The wait binds one head (--expect-head, or the local HEAD when the cwd is on the PR branch and pushed) and stops with exit 12 if the head moves; the merge is pinned to that head and runs pr merge's policy checks. Never merges on red CI (exit 10, with the diagnosis), no checks or a conflict (13), a stall (14), a moved head (12) or a merge refusal (error: MERGE_BLOCKED exit 9 or 6, HEAD_MOVED 9). Run it like ci wait: in the background on the main thread; in a subagent in the foreground with --foreground (the ghx hook arranges both), re-running the identical command on exit 15. --dry-run waits, then plans the merge without sending it.

Flags:

- `--expect-head <string>`: Land only this head (7–40 hex): wait for the PR to reach it; default the local HEAD when on the PR branch and pushed
- `--method <merge|squash|rebase>`: merge (default: merge.method); squash or rebase only when config allows
- `--override <string>` (repeatable): Overridable blocker codes the user accepted (CODE or CODE,CODE); needs --reason
- `--reason <string>`: Why the override is allowed (who asked); one line, ≤200 chars
- `--delete-branch`: Delete the same-repo head branch after merging (default: merge.deleteBranch); remote ref only
- `--foreground` (default `false`): Return pending (exit 15) after 9 min, under the Bash tool cap (a subagent); re-run the identical command

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Examples:

- `ghx pr land 3301 -R owner/repo`: Main thread: run with run_in_background: true
- `ghx pr land --foreground owner/repo#12`: Subagent: foreground; re-run on exit 15
- `ghx pr land owner/repo#12 --expect-head 9f2c4e1`: Land exactly 9f2c4e1, after a push

Schema: `ghx pr land --schema`.

## ghx pr merge

Merge when policy allows, pinned to the evaluated head; every blocker reported together

`ghx pr merge <pr> [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 3m (max 10m).

Runs the same checks as ghx pr status merge.ready, then merges with REST PUT pulls/N/merge pinned to the evaluated head. MERGE_BLOCKED lists every blocker: exit 9 when all are GitHub state (wait or fix, then re-run), 6 when a ghx policy refused (ask the user; --override CODE --reason "…" only if they accept). Squash or rebase only with an explicit --method that config allows. --dry-run prints the exact PUT.

Flags:

- `--expect-head <string>`: Refuse with HEAD_MOVED unless the head is this SHA (7–40 hex)
- `--method <merge|squash|rebase>`: merge (default: merge.method); squash or rebase only when config allows
- `--override <string>` (repeatable): Overridable blocker codes the user accepted (CODE or CODE,CODE); needs --reason
- `--reason <string>`: Why the override is allowed (who asked); one line, ≤200 chars
- `--delete-branch`: Delete the same-repo head branch after merging (default: merge.deleteBranch); remote ref only

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Replaces: `gh pr merge`, `gh pr merge --match-head-commit`, `gh api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/merge`.

Examples:

- `ghx pr merge 3301 -R powerhouse-inc/powerhouse --expect-head 9f2c4e1`: Merge, pinned to 9f2c4e1
- `ghx pr merge owner/repo#12 --dry-run`: Every check and the exact PUT, without merging
- `ghx pr merge 12 --override AUTHOR_NOT_VIEWER --reason "user asked in chat"`: Merge someone else's PR because the user asked
- `ghx pr merge 12 --expect-head 9f2c4e1 --delete-branch`: Merge, then delete the remote head branch

Schema: `ghx pr merge --schema`.

## ghx pr ready

Mark a PR ready for review, or back to draft with --undo; any PR, no ghx block needed

`ghx pr ready <pr> [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

Toggles draft through GraphQL and reads it back. A PR already in the wanted state is a no-op (changed: false). Works on PRs ghx did not open; for other edits use ghx pr edit.

Flags:

- `--undo`: Convert the PR back to a draft (gh pr ready --undo)
- `--draft`: Same as --undo

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Replaces: `gh pr ready`.

Examples:

- `ghx pr ready octo/demo#12`: mark it ready for review
- `ghx pr ready 12 --undo`: convert it back to a draft

Schema: `ghx pr ready --schema`.

## ghx pr resolve

Set the status of findings or preconditions (append-only event; resolves the review thread)

`ghx pr resolve <pr> <ids…> [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

addressed needs --commit (in the PR); wontfix, deferred, met and withdrawn need --note. Ids come from ghx pr feedback. An inline finding gets a thread reply and its thread resolved; others get one issue comment. GitHub lists only the first 250 commits of a PR, so a --commit beyond them cannot be verified and is refused.

Flags:

- `--status <addressed|wontfix|deferred|open|met|withdrawn|unmet>` (required): Findings: addressed|wontfix|deferred|open; preconditions: met|withdrawn|unmet
- `--commit <string>`: The fix commit (required for addressed); must be in the PR
- `--note <string>`: One line, ≤200 chars (required for wontfix, deferred, met, withdrawn)
- `--tracking <string>`: Issue tracking deferred work: #N or owner/repo#N

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Examples:

- `ghx pr resolve octo/demo#7 f_h4x8pz --status addressed --commit bbbbbbb`: after pushing the fix
- `ghx pr resolve 7 f_n2c6rv --status wontfix --note "The id is logged one frame up."`
- `ghx pr resolve 7 c_a1b2c3 --status met --note "Ops confirmed the window."`: a manual precondition

Schema: `ghx pr resolve --schema`.

## ghx pr review

Post a review: verdict, inline findings in the diff, hidden blocks, pinned to the head

`ghx pr review <pr> [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

Write {verdict, summary, scope?, findings[]} with your file tool and pass --input review.json. A finding goes inline only inside a diff hunk (else in the body, FINDING_NOT_INLINE). On your own PR the verdict posts as COMMENT (VERDICT_DOWNGRADED). --expect-head pins the head (HEAD_MOVED).

Flags:

- `--expect-head <string>`: Refuse with HEAD_MOVED unless the head is this SHA

JSON-only fields: `verdict`, `summary`, `scope`, `findings`.

Input: JSON input is required: write it to a file, then ghx pr review --input file.json (or --input -).

Replaces: `gh pr review`.

Examples:

- `ghx pr review octo/demo#7 --input -`: or --input review.json
- `ghx pr review 7 --input review.json --expect-head 9f2c4e1`: refuse if the head moved

Schema: `ghx pr review --schema`.

## ghx pr status

One object: description, block, merge readiness, CI for the head, feedback, preconditions, stack

`ghx pr status <pr…> [flags]`

read, single document, timeout 2m (max 5m).

Answers "can this PR land, and what is left" in one call. merge.ready is exactly what ghx pr merge would decide now (same policy engine); merge.blockers say why not. CI is reported for the head SHA only. Feedback from all three GitHub sources is folded; bodies are capped, and the full text is in ghx pr feedback. Several PRs (up to 10) give {results: [...]}, one object per PR in argument order, read concurrently, each within its share of the deadline. A PR that cannot be read, or not within its share (TIMEOUT), is {selector, ref, error} there, and the exit is 7 when some failed. With --fields or --brief, the 16 KB budget is measured on what they keep.

Flags:

- `--compare-main` (default `true`): Compare failing checks with the default branch; --no-compare-main skips it
- `--wait-mergeable` (default `true`): Retry an UNKNOWN mergeable for up to 20 s (less near the deadline); --no-wait-mergeable reads it once

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Replaces: `gh pr view`, `gh pr checks`, `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviews,comments`.

Examples:

- `ghx pr status 3301 -R powerhouse-inc/powerhouse`: Everything about PR #3301
- `ghx pr status owner/repo#12 --no-compare-main`: Skip the comparison with the default branch
- `ghx pr status 12 --no-wait-mergeable`: Read mergeable once, even if GitHub says UNKNOWN
- `ghx pr status 3264 3267 3268 -R owner/repo`: Several PRs in one call: {results: [...]}

Schema: `ghx pr status --schema`.

## ghx uninstall

Remove what ghx install added to Claude Code settings and CLAUDE.md (try --dry-run).

`ghx uninstall [flags]`

write, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

Removes only what ghx install added, as its install record (kept beside its backups in the user config dir) shows: the ghx PreToolUse hook, the deny rules it added (never your identical ones), the GHX_HOOK_MODE it set (restoring any earlier value), containers it created once empty, the marked CLAUDE.md block, and the <dir>/ghx link install made (found from the record, or given with --bin-dir). Every other setting stays. A file still exactly as ghx last wrote it gets its original bytes back from the backup. An install from before the record is judged from its <file>.bak-ghx-* backups. Backs up each changed file; a file ghx created and leaves empty is removed. --dry-run returns unified diffs and writes nothing.

Flags:

- `--scope <user|project>` (default `"user"`): user (~/.claude) or project (repo .claude/settings.local.json)
- `--bin-dir <string>`: Remove <dir>/ghx if it links to ghx (default: the link ghx install recorded, if any)
- `--snippet` (default `true`): Remove the CLAUDE.md block; --no-snippet leaves it

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Examples:

- `ghx uninstall --dry-run`: Show the diffs first
- `ghx uninstall --bin-dir ~/.local/bin`

Schema: `ghx uninstall --schema`.

## ghx version

Print the ghx version, Node version and platform (no gh calls).

`ghx version`

read, single document, timeout 1m (max 5m).

Input: Flags and positionals only; --input file.json is also accepted.

Examples:

- `ghx version`

Schema: `ghx version --schema`.
